problem:
The number of heads facing upward after tossing $3$ fair coins follows the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below. What is the expected value of the number of heads facing upward after tossing the $3$ coins?

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ |

activity_context.topic_title: Expected Values of Discrete Random Variables

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Expected Value for a Random Variable with Non-Uniform Probability
examples.problem:
The rolls of an unfair tetrahedral die follow the probability mass function $f(x)$ as shown in the table below. What is the expected value of one roll of the die?

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\dfrac{1}{10}$ | $\dfrac{3}{10}$ | $\dfrac{2}{5}$ | $\dfrac{1}{5}$ |
examples.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\textrm E[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x \cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{10})+2(\frac{3}{10})+3(\frac{2}{5})+4(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}+\frac{6}{10}+\frac{6}{5}+\frac{4}{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}+\frac{6}{10}+\frac{12}{10}+\frac{8}{10} \\  & =\frac{1+6+12+8}{10} \\  & =\frac{27}{10} \\  & =2.7\,.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Let $X$ be the first digit of the serial number of the part. Then the support is $S={2,3,4,5,6,7,8},$ and the corresponding probabilities are all $\frac{1}{7}:$

$$
f(2)=f(3)=…=f(8)=\frac{1}{7}
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+…+8\cdot f(8) \\  & =2(\frac{1}{7})+3(\frac{1}{7})+…+8(\frac{1}{7}) \\  & =\frac{2}{7}+\frac{3}{7}+…+\frac{8}{7} \\  & =\frac{2+3+4+5+6+7+8}{7} \\  & =\frac{35}{7} \\  & =5\,.\end{aligned}
$$
